properties.description:

duration for the following rivers in Colorado...

Rio Grande Near Del Norte affecting Rio Grande County.

flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande near Del Norte.

* WHEN...Until Monday morning.

evening.

feet on 06/18/1995.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 1:52PM MDT until October 24 at 4:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues along the
Rio Grande and downstream waterways.

* WHERE...Southeastern Mineral County and Rio Grande County...

* WHEN...Until 415 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will continue along and near the Rio Grande this
afternoon, especially from near Del Norte to below Monte Vista.
Several roads remain closed and housing areas evacuated due to high
water. While many rivers and streams have crested this morning,
flooding and high flows will continue into the afternoon,
especially around Monte Vista.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 143 PM MDT, Water levels along the Rio Grande remain high,
especially in the stretch from Del Norte to below Monte Vista,
although the river has crested and levels are forecast to slowly
fall through the day.
- Highway 285 between Monte Vista and Center remains closed, and
Highway 112 between Del Norte and Center is closed as well.
Please continue to heed any road closures.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
The Rio Grande from Del Norte to Monte Vista.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 24 at 3:35PM EDT until October 26 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the
High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 12 feet
expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint Lucie, Coastal
Martin, Mainland Southern Brevard and Southern Brevard Barrier
Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening. For the
High Surf Advisory, from 8 PM this evening to 8 PM EDT Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 2 AM Sunday to 8 PM EDT
Monday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Significant shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 24 at 1:29PM MDT until October 25 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, and northeast New
Mexico, including the following areas, in central New Mexico, Upper
Tularosa Valley. In east central New Mexico, Curry County, Quay
County and Roosevelt County. In northeast New Mexico, Harding
County and Union County.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and thunderstorms will expand in coverage though the
afternoon. Rainfall rates in excess of 1 inch per hour may cause
flash flooding on already saturated soils. Arroyos, small streams
and channels may quickly rise with water from heavy rainfall.
Repeated rounds of storms will increase the risk for flash
flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ; Navajo, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 12:27PM MST until October 26 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until midnight MST Sunday Night /100 AM MDT Monday/.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is imminent or
occurring. Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1222 PM MST /122 PM MDT/, water levels have crested at Winslow
and are expected to fall through the day today. However,
downstream impacts will continue at Birdsprings through at least
Sunday.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Little Colorado River, Canyon Diablo Wash, Jacks Canyon, Coyote
Wash, Clear Creek and Cottonwood Wash. Flooding is occurring
along the Little Colorado River.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 12:00pm MST /1:00pm MDT/ the stage was 18.39 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: The river has crested and now is falling.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Leupp, Birdsprings, Sunrise, Bushman Acres, Homolovi Ruins State
Park and Clear Creek Reservoir.
- This includes the following highways...
Interstate 40 between mile markers 257 and 258. Business
Interstate 40 near mile marker 257. State Route 87 near mile
marker 346.

This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Homolovi State Park Campground.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of rivers are unstable and
unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous. Do not attempt to cross
flooded roads. Find an alternate route.
